correctness.rationale: For each centrally symmetric Platonic solid, the support function on one vertex normal cell is R cos(theta). Unit edge length gives sin(delta)=1/(2R), and the regular spherical q-gon cell splits into q congruent sectors with tan(theta_b)=tan(delta)/cos(psi). The resulting second-moment integral has an elementary antiderivative. Exact special-angle substitutions give the cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron entries. The tetrahedron entry is Finch's published exact evaluation, materially inspected in full text. The bundled checker independently verifies coordinates, the sector integral, and direct support-function quadrature.

value.rationale: The five Platonic solids form the canonical complete family of regular convex polyhedra. Completing a natural random-projection invariant across all five is a natural finite classification. The result also supplies one exact normal-fan formula that handles all four centrally symmetric cases, so the dodecahedral completion is structural rather than a disconnected numerical calculation.
